overview: Pro Medicus is an Australian healthcare informatics company that develops and sells enterprise medical imaging software, principally its cloud-native Visage 7 radiology/cardiology viewer, PACS and archive platform, plus the Visage RIS radiology information system used mainly in Australia. The company sells to hospitals, academic medical centres, integrated delivery networks (IDNs), private radiology groups and teleradiology companies across Australia, North America and Europe, with North America now the dominant and fastest-growing region. It is debt-free, highly profitable, and FY26 revenue of A$261.7m (A$273.5m constant currency) generated underlying profit before tax of A$205.2m.

business_model.summary: Pro Medicus earns most of its revenue from long-term (typically 5-10 year) enterprise contracts for Visage 7, overwhelmingly priced on a transaction/usage ('pay-per-view') basis per image study read, rather than upfront perpetual licences. This converts hospital imaging volumes directly into highly predictable, high-margin recurring revenue with built-in organic growth as transaction volumes and go-lives ramp over the contract life, supplemented by minimum revenue guarantees. Visage RIS in Australia is sold on a more traditional licence/support basis. Minimum contracted revenue over the next five years stood at A$1.3bn at FY26 year-end, up 41% year on year, giving strong forward visibility.

revenue_streams.name: Australia (Visage RIS plus Visage 7, licence + transaction)
Europe (Visage 7, transaction-based, R&D hub in Berlin)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise - large academic medical centres, integrated delivery networks (IDNs), specialist/paediatric/cancer hospitals, government hospitals, private radiology groups and teleradiology providers
business_model.geographic_mix: North America grew 24.0% YoY in FY26 (30.3% constant currency) and is now the largest and fastest growing segment; Europe grew 37.2% YoY (34.9% constant currency) on the back of the Heidelberg win; Australia grew 7.3% YoY and remains the most mature, lower-growth market

main_competitors: GE HealthCare (now including Intelerad, acquired ~US$2.3bn, completed March 2026)
competitive_position.market_position: Premium, high-end share leader in large US academic medical centre and IDN radiology PACS; management estimates ~11% share of the ~690 million annual US radiology exam TAM (with ~85% of that market commercially addressable), implying significant runway; the company states 11 of the top 20 US hospitals (US News) and 4 of the world's top 10 hospitals (Newsweek) are standardised on Visage 7; KLAS research ranks Visage second (behind Sectra) for net-new PACS selections in recent years

moat_factors.description: Proprietary streaming architecture sends only the pixels needed rather than compressing and transferring whole studies, giving materially faster image access as file sizes grow (2-3GB to 6-10GB+ per study) - a structural edge over 'compress-and-send' competitors
Multi-year (5-10yr) enterprise contracts deeply embedded in clinical workflow; company reports a 100% client retention record and renewals are consistently at higher per-transaction fees and minimums

Wins in open tenders judged on feature/function/performance rather than price; deployed at elite academic centres (Mass General Brigham, NYU Langone, Trinity Health) that serve as reference sites and clinical research partners
Workforce combining specialist imaging software engineering with radiology domain knowledge is scarce and slow to replace (FY26 voluntary turnover only 2.1%)
Smaller on-premise hardware footprint and cloud-native design reduce customers' total IT cost versus legacy PACS, supporting a pricing premium

GPU-based streaming architecture is natively AI-capable; positions Visage as the delivery layer for internally built, partner (EchoIQ, Elucid, 4D Medical) and third-party AI algorithms, deepening workflow lock-in

weaknesses: Small, concentrated customer base relative to total revenue - loss or non-renewal of a single very large IDN contract would be material

Narrow addressable market at the very top end: only 4 of the top 25 US hospital networks currently run Visage, and the largest, highest-profile deals may become scarcer/lumpier as the biggest systems are already penetrated
Heavy and growing USD/EUR revenue exposure translating into AUD reporting currency, creating FX volatility in reported (though not underlying local-currency) results

Reliance on a small senior leadership/founder group (Hupert, Hall) and recent key executive turnover (new CFO, new Chief Strategy Officer, new Head of IR in FY26) raises succession-planning importance
Revenue/contract announcements are lumpy and headline-driven, which can produce sharp share price swings on perceived 'slow quarters' even when underlying volumes are growing

growth_drivers: Ongoing ramp of already-won but not-yet-fully-live North American contracts (e.g., Trinity Health, UCHealth) converting into transaction revenue as go-lives proceed

Continued new contract wins in North America across academic medical centres, IDNs, private radiology groups and teleradiology - FY26 alone added 9 new NA contracts plus the Heidelberg win in Europe, totalling A$407m TCV, plus A$141m of renewals

Cross-sell of 'full stack plus' - customers adding Visage 7 Cardiology, Digital Pathology and (from H1 CY2027) AI-optimised Reporting onto existing Viewer/Archive/Workflow deployments, raising revenue per customer
Secular shift to cloud-native PACS (CloudPACS) - all new North American contracts in FY26 were cloud-based, and health systems are consolidating multiple point solutions onto a single platform
Growing exam/file sizes (2-3GB to 6-10GB+) that structurally favour Visage's streaming architecture over compress-and-send competitors

AI monetisation - curated suite of internally developed, clinically co-developed and third-party AI algorithms (EchoIQ cardiology, Elucid, FDA-pending breast cancer detection with NYU Langone) delivered natively through Visage, plus strategic investments in 4D Medical (A$182m fair value stake) and EchoIQ (A$10m convertible note, upsizable to A$20m) as optionality on the AI ecosystem
European expansion beyond the German base following the University Hospital Heidelberg/DKFZ win
Expansion of Visage beyond radiology into broader enterprise imaging and other specialties (cardiology already underway; digital pathology newly launched)
Still-low US penetration (~11% of an estimated 690 million exam TAM, ~85% commercially addressable) leaving a long runway for market share gains

business.description: A small number of very large, multi-year IDN/health-system contracts represent a disproportionate share of incremental revenue; non-renewal or delayed go-live of a major contract would be felt quickly
Agfa, Sectra, Philips and a newly combined GE HealthCare-Intelerad are all investing in competing consolidated cloud imaging platforms; KLAS data shows Sectra leading net-new PACS selections

Business built around co-founders Hupert and Hall and a small senior team; FY26 saw new CFO, Chief Strategy Officer and Head of IR appointments, underscoring the importance of the company's stated succession-planning focus
New wins and renewals are disclosed deal-by-deal and the market has previously read 'quiet' periods as business deterioration, creating share-price volatility unrelated to underlying fundamentals

financial.description: Growing USD- and EUR-denominated revenue translated into AUD reporting currency; FY26 FX moves reduced reported revenue growth by roughly 5.5 percentage points (28.4% constant currency vs 22.9% reported) despite no debt and partial natural hedging from NA/European cost bases

financial.risk: Mark-to-market swings from strategic equity stakes
financial.description: A$182m fair value 4D Medical stake and other AI investments introduce non-operating fair-value volatility into reported (though not underlying) NPAT - FY26 reported NPAT of A$265.3m included a large unrealised fair value gain, and the 4D Medical share price had already fallen ~18% by the FY26 report date, cutting that stake's fair value by ~A$33m

regulatory.description: AI-enabled products (e.g., breast cancer detection algorithm pending FDA 510(k) clearance) must navigate evolving, jurisdiction-specific regulatory pathways (FDA in the US, the EU AI Act in Europe) before commercial release, creating approval-timeline risk for monetising the AI pipeline
Must maintain HIPAA/GDPR compliance across all markets; the company reports no known breaches to date but handles large volumes of sensitive patient imaging data

Healthcare IT is a frequent cyberattack target; PME maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation and incident response procedures but a successful breach at a company handling diagnostic imaging for major hospital systems could cause reputational and contractual damage

macro.risk: Hospital/health-system capital and IT budget cycles
macro.description: Large enterprise imaging contracts require significant customer capital commitment and procurement cycles; a tightening in US hospital system budgets or interest-rate-driven capex caution could slow the pace of new tenders, though existing transaction-based revenue is largely volume- (not budget-) driven
A stronger Australian dollar mechanically reduces reported AUD growth even when underlying local-currency performance is strong, as seen in FY26

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Enterprise medical imaging/PACS software is a structurally growing, cloud-migrating segment of health IT, driven by rising imaging volumes, larger file sizes, EMR mandates, remote/home radiology reporting, and the broader shift of hospital IT infrastructure to public cloud; consolidation among legacy vendors (e.g., GE HealthCare's 2026 acquisition of Intelerad) signals both competitive intensity and validation of the enterprise-imaging thesis
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low - revenue is driven by recurring healthcare imaging volumes (largely non-discretionary, demand-inelastic) rather than consumer or broad economic cycles, though new contract signing pace can be affected by hospital capital/IT budget cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (debt-free, net cash-generative); some indirect sensitivity via customers' capex/budget decisions and via equity valuation multiple compression in a higher-rate environment given the stock's high growth-multiple rating
key_input_costs: Skilled software engineering/R&D talent (Melbourne, Berlin, New York, San Diego)
Foreign currency translation (USD, EUR revenue into AUD reporting)

recent_developments.event: A$43m, 7-year contract win with Virtua Health (US), rollout from late 2027; continued steady cadence of new North American contract announcements into FY27

FY26 full-year results: revenue up 22.9% to A$261.7m (28.4% constant currency), reported NPAT up 130.3% to A$265.3m (boosted by 4D Medical/EchoIQ unrealised fair value gains), underlying NPAT up ~24%, final dividend 37c (full year 69c, +25.5%), ten new contracts worth A$407m TCV plus A$141m of renewals in the year, minimum 5-year contracted revenue up 41% to A$1.3bn; shares rose sharply on the result

Signed Master Agreement for an A$10m convertible note investment in ASX-listed AI cardiology company EchoIQ (with an option for a further A$10m on FDA clearance of EchoSolv HF), and agreed to become a reseller of the EchoSolv suite
Signed a 7-year, A$90m 'full stack' cloud contract with Beth Israel Lahey Health (Massachusetts) - the company's second-largest contract to date
Signed a 10-year, A$170m contract with UCHealth (Colorado) for full stack plus Cardiology - the company's largest contract to date
Won a 5-year, A$10m contract with University Hospital Heidelberg/DKFZ (Germany), driving 37.2% European revenue growth in FY26

Multiple further North American wins and renewals including Radiology Associates of North Texas, Roswell Park, Vancouver Clinic, BayCare, University of Maryland, TidalHealth, plus renewals at FMOL, Medstar, Zwanger-Pesiri, Northwestern Health, Allegheny and Ohio State University, several at increased per-transaction fees/minimums
GE HealthCare completed its ~US$2.3bn acquisition of Intelerad (closed March 2026), consolidating a key competitor and underscoring sector consolidation

A$10m strategic equity investment in ASX-listed AI company 4D Medical; fair value of the stake reached A$182.0m at 30 June 2026 before declining to ~A$149.1m by mid-August 2026 as 4D Medical's share price fell

CFO transition - Danny [surname] appointed CFO, progressing internally from Head of Finance; new Chief Strategy Officer (Tim Kern, ex-ResMed/TPG) and Head of Investor Relations (Garry Sherriff, ex-RBC) also joined during FY26/FY27, refreshing the senior leadership bench

items.target: No specific numeric FY27 revenue or NPAT guidance disclosed
items.notes: Pro Medicus does not issue formal point/range earnings guidance; the FY26 Annual Report's 'Into the Future/Outlook' section instead describes qualitative drivers: increased revenue from previously won transaction-based contracts coming on stream in FY27, continued strong North American sales pipeline, and market dynamics (cloud, AI, rising image file sizes) favouring continued Visage 7 adoption

items.period: as at FY2026 year-end, covering next 5 years
items.notes: Up 41% year-on-year from the prior year's minimum contracted revenue base, reflecting new contract wins and renewals signed during FY26

items.target: North American commercial release scheduled for H1 calendar 2027 (already in production in Europe)
items.notes: New revenue-generating product (alongside Digital Pathology and Cardiology) expected to contribute from FY27 and beyond per management commentary

items.target: First AASB S2 mandatory climate disclosures
items.notes: Company is a 'Group 2' reporting entity under Australian climate disclosure rules, commencing reporting from 1 July 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman and CEO described FY26 as 'another very good year' with 'strong, profitable growth' despite a 'challenging foreign currency backdrop,' citing record new sales (10 contracts worth A$407m) and 100% client retention on renewals. Management flagged the North American business's continued momentum (revenue +24.0% reported / +30.3% constant currency) and reiterated confidence that secular trends (cloud migration, AI, rising image data volumes) will continue to support growth into FY27 and beyond, while noting the company remains debt-free with A$252.3m in cash/deposits/financial assets to fund organic growth.

bull_case: Best-in-class, technically differentiated product (streaming architecture) with a 100% client retention record and a long runway in a large, growing North American market where management estimates only ~11% penetration of the addressable exam volume

Highly visible, high-margin, transaction-based recurring revenue model with minimum contracted revenue of A$1.3bn over the next five years (up 41% YoY), largely insulating the core business from near-term macro shocks

Debt-free balance sheet with A$252m+ in cash/financial assets, strong operating cash conversion (A$127.5m FY26 operating cash flow), and a growing, fully franked dividend (69c FY26, +25.5%), giving ample capacity to fund R&D, AI investments and shareholder returns without dilution

Multiple embedded growth vectors beyond core PACS - Cardiology, Digital Pathology, AI-optimised Reporting and third-party AI reseller deals (EchoIQ) - that raise average revenue per customer from an already-won, sticky installed base

Track record of consistently winning large, competitive enterprise tenders on technical merit (not price) against bigger, better-resourced incumbents (GE HealthCare/Intelerad, Philips, Agfa, Sectra), demonstrating a durable product moat
bear_case: Very high valuation (trailing P/E roughly 65-100x depending on measure/date) prices in years of continued high growth; any deceleration in contract-win cadence or go-live timing risks sharp multiple compression, as seen in prior 2026 share-price drawdowns (down ~30-40% at points in the year before recovering)

The largest, highest-profile US academic medical centres and top hospital systems are increasingly already penetrated (11 of the top 20 US hospitals, but only 4 of the top 25 health networks), implying future large-ticket wins may become scarcer or smaller, pressuring the growth rate that supports the premium multiple

Intensifying competitive consolidation - GE HealthCare's ~US$2.3bn acquisition of Intelerad (closed March 2026) creates a larger, better-capitalised rival, and Sectra continues to lead net-new PACS vendor selections per KLAS data

Reported earnings are increasingly influenced by non-operating, volatile fair-value gains/losses on strategic equity stakes (4D Medical, EchoIQ) which can distort headline NPAT (FY26 reported NPAT +130% vs underlying +24%) and already partially reversed within weeks of the FY26 result as 4D Medical's share price fell

Growing foreign currency exposure as North America becomes an ever-larger share of revenue means reported AUD results (and consensus beats/misses) can be meaningfully affected by exchange-rate moves independent of underlying business performance
